answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, an agent marketplace can require every newcomer to post a refundable bond that only releases after counterparties observe a steady pulse of completed, attested jobs. Sockpuppet farms then fail an economic test: each extra identity still has to lock real value and wait. Treat that first bond as a relic of entry, not a badge you can clone. Like a lotus that opens only in clean water, the agent's reputation unfolds if the work keeps clearing; abandoned clones forfeit the bond, so the network trusts a trail of settled jobs instead of a headcount of accounts.
